sentences.text: The lighthouse stood on a black rock where the bay met the open water.
Before dusk, the keeper climbed the spiral stairs and wiped the great glass lens.
Salt spray had left a cloudy film, and a dirty lens would waste the light.
The keeper checked the lamp, the spare bulb, and the horn that calls through fog.
By evening a gray wall of fog had slid in from the sea.
Boats could no longer trust their eyes, so the keeper started the horn.
A deep note rolled across the water, then a pause, then the same note again.
Out in the bay, a fishing boat slowed and turned a little wider of the rock.
The keeper watched the beam sweep in a steady circle, the way it did every clear or foggy night.
The work was not a race. It was the same careful list, done on time.
When the fog thinned near dawn, the horn went quiet and the stairs were still damp.
The keeper wrote the night in the log: fog, horn working, no ships too close.
A bright lens and a working horn had given the boats a way to stay off the rocks.

questions.prompt: What is this story mostly about?

choices.text: A keeper's steady work that helps boats avoid the rocks
A fishing boat that climbs the lighthouse stairs
A lamp that only works on sunny days
A logbook that writes itself at dawn

questions.explanation: The keeper cleans the lens, checks the horn, and keeps the light turning through the fog. Protecting boats is the main idea.

questions.prompt: In this story, the lens is what?

choices.text: The rope that ties up a boat
The glass that shapes and sends the light
The ink used in the log
The fog sitting on the bay

questions.explanation: The keeper wipes the great glass lens because a dirty one would waste the light. In this story the lens is the glass that sends the beam.

questions.prompt: What does the keeper write in the log?

choices.text: Fog, horn working, no ships too close
A ship hit the black rock

questions.explanation: Near dawn the keeper writes: fog, horn working, no ships too close. That is the exact note in the log.

questions.prompt: Why does the fishing boat most likely turn wider of the rock?

choices.text: The keeper waves a flag the boat can see clearly
The fog lifts the boat out of the water
The log tells the boat where to turn
It hears the horn and uses the sound to stay away

questions.explanation: The story does not quote the people on the boat. The horn starts, a deep note rolls out, and then the boat slows and turns wider. The sound is the clue.
